baseline:
C
An infinite series is the sum of a sequence with an unlimited number of terms.

B
A convergent series is one whose sum approaches a specific finite value as more terms are added. A divergent series is one whose sum does not approach a finite value; it may grow infinitely large or oscillate.

B
The convergence of a series is defined by its sequence of partial sums approaching a limit. The distance between these partial sums and the limit is measured using the absolute value of their difference, |S_n - L|, which is the standard absolute value metric on the real numbers.

B
In the 2-adic metric, the distance between two numbers, x and y, is determined by the 2-adic norm of their difference, |x - y|₂. This norm is small when the difference (x - y) is divisible by a high power of 2.

C
In p-adic number systems, a geometric series converges if the p-adic absolute value of its ratio is less than 1. For the 2-adic system, the absolute value of 2, `|2|_2`, is 1/2. Since 1/2 < 1, the series converges. Using the standard formula for the sum of a geometric series, we get `1 / (1 - 2) = -1`.
